baseline_kernel: current-source SGLang API-v1 DeepGEMM grouped masked BM128/stage-8

bottleneck.evidence: The final serving-native result captured a faster single candidate device kernel but a slower complete selected API-v1 interval, so the remaining loss is above device-kernel execution.

approaches.summary: Added an exact-descriptor, per-call BM16 auto-stage DeepGEMM specialization with a dedicated infini_kernel symbol.
approaches.why: The generic full-tile TMA epilogue overwrote invalid rows in the caller-owned output slab.

approaches.summary: Preserved invalid output rows by restoring them inside the same kernel before the full-tile store.
approaches.why: The extra read and restage work preserved ownership but overwhelmed the useful small-M work.

approaches.summary: Kept TMA for full tiles and used predicated vector stores only for valid rows in partial tiles, then deferred diagnostic counter materialization until after timing.
approaches.why: The device kernel improved, but current SGLang API-v1 selection and enqueue overhead left the complete candidate interval slower than stock.

lesson: A smaller grouped-GEMM tile can reduce padded output traffic yet still lose at the production callback boundary. Measure the complete selected interval early, and preserve caller-owned partial tiles in the kernel before spending profiling budget on stage or barrier refinements.
transfers_to: small-M grouped masked GEMMs on SM100
serving callbacks where Python selector overhead is comparable to kernel time
caveats: This was a serving-native hotspot goal, not the generated testbench glm52/moe_down_proj_decode task; structured benchmark numbers are intentionally omitted here and retained in the terminal evidence.
